cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Outsmart the Room
cards.instruction: Turn every clue, deduction, and secret into a contest you must solve or control first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Don't open the delivery email. Let me deduce where our office biscuits went. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Reception signed for them. I'll tell everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Wait. That's a clue, not a conclusion. I should announce the solution.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Too late. They're downstairs opening the box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell them nobody eats until I identify the contents. Finding a box doesn't mean they've solved the biscuits.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 blocks easy information, A3 reserves solution announcement and A5 shifts to contents, but rank language does not accommodate B practical progress.

heightening.evidence: B4 opening the box forces A5 a new first-to-identify contest.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 finding a box versus solving biscuits explains the newly invented contest; it can be replaced with a direct announcement request and a practical offer.
